properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 11 at 9:33PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

Horse Creek Near Arcadia at SR 72 affecting DeSoto County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Horse Creek near Arcadia at SR 72.

* WHEN...From late Sunday night until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, The access road to Hidden Oak is
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Friday the stage was 7.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Monday morning and continue rising to 12.3 feet Monday evening.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.3
feet on 08/09/1957.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at 100 PM EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT FROM LATE SUNDAY NIGHT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 11 at 9:20PM MST until September 12 at 12:15AM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Cochise County in southeastern Arizona...
South Central Graham County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 1215 AM MST.

* At 920 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of North Central Cochise and South Central
Graham Counties.

This includes Route 191 between mile markers 88 and 93.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Dial Wash, Gillespie Wash, Willow Spring Wash, Owl Wash, Oak Draw,
W A Wash and Ash Creek.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 11 at 8:58PM MST until September 12 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The West Fire scar in...
Gila County in east central Arizona...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until midnight MST.

* At 858 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the West Fire scar. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of
rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in Webber Creek.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the West Fire scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
West Fire scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Geronimo Estates and Flowing Springs.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Geronimo Boy Scout Camp.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
West Webber Creek.
properties.instruction:
Flash flooding is occurring or imminent downstream of the West Fire
scar, including areas along Webber Creek. Campers and hikers should
move to higher ground immediately! Stay away from creeks and washes!

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 11 at 6:13PM MST until September 11 at 11:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Gila County in east central Arizona...
Navajo County in north central Arizona...

* Until 1115 PM MST.

* At 613 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain in the upper portions of Canyon Creek. Between 2 and 4
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1
inch are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks, streams, and
normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Chediski Mountain and Chediski Peak.

This includes State Route 288 near mile marker 311.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Valentine Ridge Campground.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Canyon Creek, Cibecue Creek, Bear Creek, Carrizo Creek, and Salt
Creek.
properties.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

Get out of washes and creeks if you are camping or hiking! Flooding
is occurring or imminent and will inundate creeks and washes.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 11 at 10:03PM MST until September 11 at 10:30PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
SVRPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Gila County in east central Arizona...
Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* Until 1030 PM MST.

* At 1002 PM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located over Sycamore
Creek, and is nearly stationary.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Sunflower and Sycamore Creek.

This includes AZ Route 87 between mile markers 218 and 228.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Large hail, damaging wind, and continuous cloud to ground lightning
are occurring with this storm. Move indoors immediately. Lightning is
one of nature's leading killers. Remember, if you can hear thunder,
you are close enough to be struck by lightning.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 11 at 11:56PM CDT until September 12 at 12:15AM CDT by NWS Paducah KY
properties.description:
At 1156 PM CDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from
over Grayville to near Darmstadt, or along a line from 9 miles south
of Albion to 9 miles northwest of Evansville, moving northeast at 35
mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

This severe thunderstorm will be near...
Grayville, Cynthiana, Poseyville and Blairsville around 1200 AM
CDT.
Owensville around 1205 AM CDT.

Other locations impacted by the severe thunderstorm include Griffin.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. These storms are capable of producing damaging winds.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 11 at 6:20PM MST until September 11 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Gila County in east central Arizona...

* Until 1100 PM MST.

* At 620 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated that the heavy rain had
ended over the Fossil Creek area. However, flash flooding remains a
threat from earlier thunderstorms producing heavy rain upstream of
Fossil Creek and Hardscrabble Creek near Strawberry. Between 2 and
4 inches of rain have fallen. Flooding impacts will continue, but
no additional rainfall is expected. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, and
normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
The Toilet Bowl, Fossil Creek Waterfall, Fossil Creek Day Use Area,
Strawberry and Fossil Springs Wilderness.

This includes State Route 87 between mile markers 271 and 272.

This includes the following swimming holes...
All swimming holes and waterfalls on Fossil Creek and Fossil Creek
Dam "The Toilet Bowl".

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Fossil Creek and Hardscrabble Creek.
properties.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Get out of washes and creeks if you are camping or hiking! Flooding
is occurring or imminent and will inundate creeks and washes.
